messages:
Eli: thanks for today reopening a short thread for any strategy / competitive questions we didnt get to. post quick ones here.
Maya: framing: our north star = predictable, production-grade inference (latency SLOs, repeatable rollouts, and transparent unit economics). not a model shop 1 we optimize serving.
Jordan: practical example: same API + rollout primitives across hosted/dedicated/private so customers can migrate without rewrites. thats the "unified runtime" promise.
Priya: sales question: how do we position vs hyperscalers who tout model catalogs + managed endpoints?
Maya: call out scenarios where hypers are weakest: private (VPC/on-prem) installs, fine-grained rollbacks, prefix/KV caching, and token-level cost visibility. those are procurement blockers for many customers.
Tomas: product follow-up: can we provide a one-liner for decks? e.g., "Redwood: predictable inference where reliability and unit economics matter"?
Eli: yes, that works. maybe add: "Same API. Same SLAs. No surprises."
Rachel: marketing ask: customers ask about model quality 1 how do we avoid sounding like we don't care about models?
Jordan: message: "We make your chosen model reliable and cost-effective in production." emphasize evals + rollout safety nets.
Priya: ops ask: Dedicated SLA timeline? procurement teams need dates for RFPs.
Maya: target initial 99.9% Dedicated SLA in the next fiscal quarter; runbooks and failover docs will be published with it.
Tomas: competitor nuance: what if a customer already uses cloud endpoints but is seeing cost spikes? what's our pitch?
Eli: show a concrete case: caching/batching with our runtime reduced per-token cost by X% in empirical benchmarks; also highlight transparent cost per route so they can predict spend.
AllHandsBot: poll: "Which external narrative should we prioritize next week?" options: 1) predictability & SLAs 2) unit economics at scale 3) private & compliance 4) rollout & observability. react 1/2/3/4.
Rachel: action items 1 I'll work with eng on a 1-page "why not cloud endpoints" with concrete scenarios and numbers.
Jordan: eng will scope a small reproducible benchmark repo and short guide for sales to cite.
Eli: great thread  we'll bundle these into a 2-slide lead deck + FAQ and share by end of week. keep short follow-ups here. :rocket:
